slides.1.title: Portugal's Place in the Wine World
slides.1.html:
Portugal is one of Europe's oldest wine-producing countries, with over 3,000 years of viticultural history. Although its territory is only about three times the size of Taiwan, Portugal has produced a diversity that astonishes the world.

🏅 Three Sources of Portuguese Pride

  • The world's first demarcated region under continuous regulation: the Marquis of Pombal demarcated Douro in 1756, earlier than Bordeaux in France (Chianti in 1716 and Tokaj in 1737 were demarcated even earlier, but were not subject to continuous regulation)
  • The richest native varieties: over 250 indigenous varieties, many of which are hardly found elsewhere
  • Porto and Madeira: two of the world's most famous fortified wines, with century-long ageing potential

📊 Portuguese Wine in Numbers

  • Vineyard area: about 190,000 hectares
  • Legally defined DOCs: more than 30
  • Annual production: about 700 million litres, among the world's top 10 wine-producing countries
slides.2.title: 3,000 Years of Wine History
slides.2.html:
From the vines brought by the Phoenicians to the Marquis of Pombal's creation of the world's first demarcated region under continuous regulation ——3,000 years of winemaking made Portugal one of Europe's oldest winemaking peoples, long before the rise of the New World

1000 BC
🚢 The Phoenicians introduce the vine

Sailing along the Atlantic coast, Phoenician traders brought vines to the Iberian Peninsula, establishing early vineyards in what is now southern Portugal and the Douro Valley.

13th–15th centuries
⚓ The wine trade of the Age of Discovery

Portugal became Europe's mightiest seafaring empire, and wine travelled by ship to Asia, Africa and the Americas. To survive long voyages, brandy began to be added to the wine — the beginnings of fortified wine.

1703
🤝 The Methuen Treaty

Britain and Portugal signed a trade treaty giving Portuguese wine preferential duties in the British market. Port exports surged, establishing a lasting British taste for Portuguese wine.

1756
📋 The world's first demarcated region under continuous regulation

The Marquis of Pombal formally demarcated the Douro, creating the world's first government-regulated wine region system — 99 years before the 1855 Classification of Bordeaux.

1986 to present
🌍 Joining the EU and modernisation

After joining the EU, Portugal adopted modern winemaking technology. From the 2000s, premium dry reds led by Touriga Nacional rose on the international market, and wine lovers worldwide rediscovered Portugal's diversity.

slides.3.title: Portuguese Wine: Six Core Characteristics
slides.3.items.0.label: Fresh Atlantic whites
slides.3.items.0.desc: Alvarinho from Vinho Verde: crisp, refreshing acidity with a light spritz
slides.3.items.1.label: Douro Valley terraces
slides.3.items.1.desc: The schist terraces of the UNESCO-listed Douro: steep, spectacular and the birthplace of Port
slides.3.items.2.label: Porto (Port)
slides.3.items.2.desc: The world's most famous fortified sweet wine, with a rich variety of Tawny, Ruby and Vintage styles
slides.3.items.3.label: Madeira
slides.3.items.3.desc: Oxidative fortified wine from an Atlantic volcanic island, able to age for over a century
slides.3.items.4.label: A treasury of native varieties
slides.3.items.4.desc: 250+ indigenous varieties including Touriga Nacional, Alvarinho and Encruzado
slides.3.items.5.label: Sun-soaked southern reds
slides.3.items.5.desc: Alentejo's hot, continental-leaning climate yields round, rich, modern-style reds
slides.4.question: In which country is the world's first wine region demarcated by government and continuously regulated (1756)?
slides.4.explanation: In 1756 Portugal's Marquis of Pombal founded the Companhia Geral da Agricultura das Vinhas do Alto Douro and formally demarcated the Douro under continuous regulation, making it the world's first regulated wine region (Chianti in 1716 and Tokaj in 1737 were demarcated earlier but were not subject to continuous regulation).
